obligations.statement: Every admitted exchange or journal effect nets to zero in every unit, and so does every book built only through the core posting primitives.
obligations.owner: norn.core physics pack; kernel accounting-leg commit check
assumptions: Amounts are exact integers at one declared precision per unit.
Value moves only through types that declare an accounting leg; an undeclared type is a marked boundary where the inherited claim stops.
counterexamples: a two-leg journal debiting 100 and crediting 90 is admitted
100 EGP balanced against -100 USD
a workflow posts each half of an exchange in a separate unbalanced journal

obligations.statement: No admitted operation edits or removes a posted economic event or journal entry; each admitted operation only adds entries.
obligations.owner: norn.core physics pack; kernel accounting-leg commit check
assumptions: The ledger is the only writer of posted entries.
counterexamples: an update to a posted leg is committed
a posted leg is deleted through an unmarked ancestor type

obligations.statement: A correction is a new entry linked to its posted original with exactly negated legs, so the pair nets to zero on every account and unit; an entry is reversed at most once and a reversal is never reversed.
assumptions: A partial correction is a full reversal followed by a new posting.
counterexamples: a reversal with a different amount than its original
two reversals of one original
a reversal of a reversal

obligations.statement: For one resource in one unit, stock received equals stock issued plus stock on hand; a transformation issues its inputs and receives its outputs, so the law holds per resource.
obligations.owner: norn.core physics pack; kernel quantity ledger
assumptions: Quantities are exact and in one unit per balance partition; conversions are separate balanced postings.
counterexamples: a transfer that debits one location without crediting another
a transformation output with no recorded consumption

obligations.statement: Holds (escrow, reservations, quota use) are never negative and never exceed the balance they are held against, so available quantity is never negative.
obligations.owner: norn.core physics pack; kernel quantity ledger
assumptions: Every hold, release and consumption goes through the quantity ledger in one cell transaction.
counterexamples: two reservations each fit the available stock but together exceed it
releasing more than is held

obligations.statement: A commitment ends fulfilled, cancelled or breached and is never dropped: terminal states are absorbing, no operation removes a commitment, and once its due time passes the deadline event ends it.
obligations.owner: norn.core physics pack; cell clock deadline timer
assumptions: The cell clock raises the deadline event for every open commitment once its due time is reached (timer fairness).
counterexamples: a promised commitment past its due time that is neither fulfilled nor breached
a cancelled commitment reopened
a commitment row deleted while open

obligations.statement: The value of stock issued is computed by the resource's declared valuation method, and inventory value equals value received less value issued under every method. The method is a parameter of the law, not a variant of it.

parameter.setBy: tenant, as a governed and audited change

assumptions: Quantity conservation holds for the resource (INV-CORE-QUANTITY-CONSERVATION).
Rounding of moving-average unit cost is declared and exact.
counterexamples: an issue valued by a method other than the declared one
a method change that revalues past issues
moving-average rounding that leaves a residual between inventory value and its ledger account

obligations.statement: No type is both a commitment and a claim (Commitment ⊓ Claim = ∅). A claim arises from a fulfilled or accepted commitment through givesRiseTo, recorded on the claim as arises_from.
obligations.owner: norn.core physics pack; checker consistency rules
assumptions: Types reach the primitives only through implements and interface extends.
counterexamples: an order type that implements both core.Commitment and core.Claim
an invoice modelled as a commitment
